raw_response:
I've been working this land for fifty years. I know every corner of it. At 73, just me and my wife at home now, I can't push as hard as I used to, so I plan carefully. My 4.1 mu is enough — the cotton brings in cash, the mungbean fills in the rows between the cotton and puts something back in the soil, and the millet keeps us fed through winter.

**Cotton / Mungbean field (~3 mu):** I plant these together the same way I always have — cotton in the main rows, mungbean in the spaces between. I use the improved cotton variety I've been getting from the township supply station these past several years, not hybrid — too expensive and I don't fully trust it. I'll do one rotary tillage pass before planting, easier on my back than ploughing. I put down base fertilizer in the ground before planting, then top-dress with urea when the cotton starts flowering. Bollworms and aphids are always a problem — I'll spray seven times or so, same as most years. The well gives me enough water. I irrigate before planting to get good germination, then again at bud, flower, boll-set, and late boll stages — five times is about right. The mungbean I don't fuss over much. I saved my own seed from last year. It takes care of itself mostly. Maybe one spray if I see something bad.

**Millet (~1.1 mu):** This is our food. I use the local variety my family has always grown. I plough this plot properly — millet does better with a good plough, I've found. Fertilizer is modest, it doesn't need much. I water it two or three times. One pesticide application if anything shows up, but usually millet is not much trouble.
